entrypoints.summary: An HTTP redirect response handled by DefaultHttpClient can specify a redirect target across a domain boundary while the original request contains Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization headers.

affected_components.role: Patched configuration defines Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie as default cross-origin filtered headers.
Advisory identifies this redirect-following client component as affected.
Redirect header-copy test file added or changed by the version-specific patches.

negative_controls: A same-origin redirect is outside the stated cross-origin filtering invariant.
No execution transcript is supplied in this bundle.
observability.positive_marker: The redirect target receives one or more of Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, or Cookie headers from the original request.

preconditions: A DefaultHttpClient request carries Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization.
The client follows a redirect to a different domain boundary.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: An HTTP redirect response whose Location identifies a target across a domain boundary.
trigger_steps.summary: Cause the client to follow a cross-origin HTTP redirect while processing a request with sensitive headers.

capabilities.concept: forward sensitive request headers to a cross-origin redirect target

impacts.concept: disclosure of HTTP credentials or session cookies to a redirect target

mitigations.concept: filter Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie on cross-origin redirects

relation_candidates.dst: forward sensitive request headers to a cross-origin redirect target
relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory describes DefaultHttpClient following redirects and forwarding these headers to targets across domain boundaries.

relation_candidates.dst: disclosure of HTTP credentials or session cookies to a redirect target
relation_candidates.rationale: Forwarding Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie values to another domain exposes those values at the redirect target.
relation_candidates.src: forward sensitive request headers to a cross-origin redirect target

relation_candidates.dst: filter Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie on cross-origin redirects
relation_candidates.rationale: All three inspected maintenance patches add those headers to redirectCrossOriginFilteredHeaders.
relation_candidates.src: forward sensitive request headers to a cross-origin redirect target

impact.affected_asset: HTTP authentication credentials, proxy credentials, and session cookies attached to the original client request.
impact.attacker_capability: A party controlling or influencing a redirect target can obtain sensitive headers forwarded by the client.
impact.security_effect: Confidentiality loss through disclosure of Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization values to a cross-origin redirect target.

causal_trace.summary: A client request contains Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization headers and receives a redirect whose target is across a domain boundary.
The redirect-copy policy did not distinguish a cross-origin target for these sensitive headers; the advisory states its blocklist filtered only Host, Connection, TE, CT, and CL.
DefaultHttpClient followed the redirect and forwarded the sensitive request headers to the redirect target.
The redirect target can receive credentials or cookies that were intended for the original origin, resulting in confidentiality loss.

failure.operation: Copying request headers while constructing/following a cross-origin redirect

primary_invariant.statement: When following a redirect to a different origin, the client must not copy Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, or Cookie headers from the original request to the redirected request.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The documented pre-patch redirect header blocklist did not include those sensitive headers, so they were forwarded across domain boundaries.

quality.review_notes: OSV and the upstream advisory directly establish the affected package, header-forwarding behavior, impact, and patched release thresholds. Inspected version-specific patches show the new cross-origin filtered-header configuration and include RedirectHeaderCopyTest in their changed files, but this bundle contains no test-run result; the unit-test oracle is therefore a contract rather than observed execution. The advisory also mentions unlimited redirect-loop DoS, but this record intentionally isolates the sensitive-header disclosure mechanism.

remediation.invariant_restored: The patches introduce a cross-origin redirect filtered-header set containing Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, and Cookie, so those headers are designated for filtering when the redirect changes origin.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: introduced in 1.2.8; the OSV ecosystem range reports a fix at 3.10.6

oracle.expected_negative: Header forwarding behavior not covered by the cross-origin sensitive-header contract, including same-origin behavior, requires separate review.
oracle.expected_positive: A redirect to a different origin does not deliver Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, or Cookie headers to the redirect target.
